title: Modal accessibility audit, VPAT evidence kit, and resilient token fallback strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Several product teams have reported inconsistent keyboard behavior and contrast regressions inside modal/dialog surfaces across density and theme variants. Previous audits touched focus order and aria-labels, but we do not have a consolidated VPAT-ready evidence kit for modal/dialog components nor a documented token fallback strategy when dynamic theming degrades contrast.

Goal: Create a comprehensive accessibility audit for all modal/dialog variants (small alerts, confirm, large app-level modals), produce VPAT evidence artifacts for certification, and ship a token fallback policy so that modal surfaces consistently meet AA contrast and deterministic focus behavior across platforms.

Scope: All modal/dialog components in the core component library (Modal, Dialog, ConfirmDialog, Sheet) and variants used in Console, Dedicated onboarding flows, and Private deployment UIs. Includes light/dark/high-contrast tokens, compact/dense forms inside modals, header/action-button groups, and embedded data tables. Excludes third-party consumer modals embedded by partners (handle separately).

Deliverables:
- Accessibility audit matrix (ARIA roles, focus order, live regions, keyboard trap/escape) for each modal variant.
- VPAT evidence artifacts (screenshots, keyboard trace videos, test logs, narrative responses) organized per VPAT section.
- Token fallback mapping: a small set of guaranteed contrast-safe tokens used when theme composition would otherwise produce < 4.5:1 for body text or < 3:1 for UI components.
- Regression harness checklist and a runnable script for QA that automates core keyboard flows and contrast checks (storybook + axe + visual snapshots).
- Design tokens patch proposal and a follow-up engineering change request with kernel-level instructions for runtime token substitution in Private deployments.

Success metrics:
- All modal variants meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast thresholds in the audit matrix.
- VPAT kit reviewed and sign-off from Compliance and Product Security.
- Automated regression checks start failing if a modal change regresses keyboard trapping/escape behavior or token contrast.

Risks & open questions:
- Some legacy modals rely on global z-index shims and portal behavior that complicates keyboard trapping — engineering time required to normalize.
- Private deployments that customize tokens may bypass runtime fallback; need to confirm we can ship a runtime substitution strategy that respects customer token overrides and KMS-managed themes.
- VPAT requires a narrative for known limitations; need Legal/Compliance alignment on wording.

Stakeholders: Design (owner), Accessibility lead (Eleni Rose), Eng owners for modal (ENG-41221) and theming runtime (ENG-43098), Compliance (Kiran Mehta), Product owners for Console and Dedicated flows.
acceptance_criteria: Audit matrix completed with explicit pass/fail per WCAG item for each modal variant
VPAT evidence kit uploaded to Confluence and linked in ticket, with Compliance review comment
Token fallback mapping documented and merged to design tokens RFC
Regression harness added to Storybook tests and a failing test demonstrated for a simulated regression
Engineering change request created with runtime substitution approach for Private deployments
